An FBI seal is displayed on a podium before a news conference in Portland, Oregon [File: Jenny Kane/AP Photo]By Al Jazeera StaffPublished On 21 Nov 202621 Nov 2026
The FBI’s national criminal database has suffered a suspected breach, according to multiple US media reports.
President Donald Trump, who has repeatedly downplayed breaches affecting departments within his administration, appeared to confirm the FBI hacking during a television interview on Saturday.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3NSA attributes US network outage to routine ‘maintenance’ activitieslist 2 of 3If hackers can take over a supermarket fridge, what else is at risk?list 3 of 3Outages in US cause worry, despite official attempts to downplay concernsend of list
“Well, we just heard about it, and I will say that it’s not good. I don’t like that,” Trump told Fox News.
On Friday, CNN and NBC reported that the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), which is used by law enforcement agencies across the United States to share information on criminal warrants and background checks, was compromised, citing two people who had been briefed on the matter.
The reported hacking, which would be the second to hit the bureau this year, is the latest in a string of US government breaches and outages that have alarmed officials over the past week.
In a separate incident, NBC reported an apparent cyberattack against the US Department of Agriculture.
The FBI and USDA did not immediately return Al Jazeera’s request for comment.
In the interview on Saturday, Trump suggested the hack of the FBI’s crucial database could be viewed with “a positive spin”.

A restaurant damaged by a Russian attack in Kryvyi Rih, Ukraine, on November 21, 2026 [Handout: Dnipropetrovsk Regional Military Administration/AP Photo]By AFP and APPublished On 21 Nov 202621 Nov 2026
A Russian attack on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s hometown of Kryvyi Rih has killed two people and wounded 60 others, according to local officials.
The strikes hit the central Ukrainian city on Friday night, killing a seven-year-old boy and a 20-year-old woman, while six children were among the injured.
Recommended Stories list of 2 itemslist 1 of 2Russian missiles hit Poland: What happened, and could NATO respond?list 2 of 2Russian crew evacuating ship hit by drones off coast of Finlandend of list
About 25 apartment buildings, a hospital, schools and businesses were damaged, according to Oleksandr Vilkul, the head of Kryvyi Rih’s city administration.
Vilkul said on Saturday that Russian forces launched further missiles after emergency workers arrived, hitting rescuers, medical personnel and utility crews.
Footage released by Ukraine’s emergency services appeared to show additional strikes during the rescue operation.
Russian attacks elsewhere in Ukraine killed two people in the southern Zaporizhia region, according to its governor.
Russian authorities also reported six deaths, including a child, from a Ukrainian attack on a residential area in Russian-controlled Luhansk, an eastern Ukrainian region.
The violence followed a separate incident on Friday in which two Russian missiles and a suspected drone landed in southeastern Poland, a member of NATO, the military alliance linking the United States, Canada and European countries.

The youth wing of India’s main opposition Congress party has staged protests outside Meta offices in three cities, demanding that the United States technology company restore the Instagram accounts of its leaders.
The protests took place in Hyderabad, Mumbai and Gurugram, near New Delhi, on Friday and led to clashes with police and security guards, according to footage released by the Indian Youth Congress on Saturday.
